steps.name: QC and align log2 expression matrix with metadata
caveats: The matrix is already log2 normalized (log2(TPM+1)) — do not re-normalize, re-log, or feed it into a count-based tool
12000 x 13 dimensions mean one column is not a sample (likely a gene identifier column) — resolve this explicitly rather than assuming
steps.question: Do the 12000x13 log2(TPM+1) expression matrix and the 12-sample metadata.csv align correctly for a 6 treated vs 6 control unpaired comparison, and what is the extra 13th column?
acceptance_criteria: Confirms which of the 13 columns in log_expr.csv are sample columns vs a gene-id column, and subsets to the 12 samples present in metadata.csv
Confirms metadata.csv assigns exactly 6 samples to treated and 6 to control with no missing/duplicate sample IDs
Reports value range of the matrix consistent with log2(TPM+1) (non-negative, typically 0-~15) and flags any sample as an outlier via PCA or hierarchical clustering
Produces a cleaned, sample-matched expression matrix and group vector ready for modeling

steps.name: limma differential expression: treated vs control
caveats: Unpaired design with n=6 per group and single batch — no batch correction term needed, no pairing/blocking variable to model
Do not apply voom (designed for raw counts) since input is already log2 normalized continuous data; use limma's trend/eBayes on the log2 matrix directly
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) muscle samples using the delivered log2(TPM+1) values?
acceptance_criteria: Fits a limma linear model (lmFit) with a treated-vs-control design matrix on the QC'd log2 matrix from T1S1, applies eBayes moderation, and extracts topTable with logFC, moderated t-statistic, raw p-value, and BH-adjusted FDR for all genes
Reports the number of genes significant at FDR < 0.05 and at FDR < 0.1, and lists the top up- and down-regulated genes by adjusted p-value
Explicitly states that count-based tools (DESeq2/edgeR) were not used because the input is pre-normalized log2 data, not raw counts
Outputs a full ranked gene table (all 12000 genes) suitable for downstream enrichment

steps.name: WikiPathways enrichment of DE gene list
caveats: WikiPathways gene sets use HGNC gene symbols — confirm the DE gene list's identifier space matches (or map it) before joining
With only 12000 genes profiled and n=6 per group, enrichment power is limited; treat borderline pathway hits cautiously
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control muscle samples?
acceptance_criteria: Confirms availability of the human WikiPathways gene set file before use; if absent, reports the gap rather than fabricating enrichment results
Runs over-representation or ranked (fgsea-style) enrichment using the full ranked gene list (logFC and FDR) from T1S2 against WikiPathways human pathway gene sets
Reports enriched pathways with adjusted p-values (BH-corrected) and the leading-edge/member genes driving each significant pathway
Interprets results in the context of muscle tissue biology, flagging any enrichment driven by very few genes as weak signal

plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE via limma on log2 data
plan.analytical_narrative: The core facility delivered log2(TPM+1) normalized expression (12000 genes x 13 samples matrix trimmed to the 12 samples with condition labels in metadata.csv: 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch), not raw counts. DESeq2/edgeR require raw integer counts and cannot be validly applied to pre-normalized log2 values — running them here would silently produce meaningless results. limma is the correct tool for continuous, already log-transformed/normalized expression data of this kind (its moderated t-test framework, via lmFit/eBayes, was designed for exactly this input type, historically for microarray log-ratios and now widely applied to log2 CPM/TPM RNA-seq data). The plan therefore: (1) loads and QC-checks the log2 matrix and metadata, confirming sample alignment and group balance; (2) fits a limma linear model with empirical Bayes moderation for the treated-vs-control contrast, producing a ranked DE gene list with logFC, moderated t, p-value, and BH-adjusted FDR; (3) runs pathway enrichment (WikiPathways human gene sets, confirmed present in the reference store) on the DE result to contextualize the affected biology in muscle tissue. No translational/PK/safety steps are added since the research question is a plain DE contrast with no drug, biomarker-outcome, or safety data present.
